WARD CHASES GURNEY
No sooner did A. J. Foyt, Houston, Tex. pass Dan Gurney, Costa Mesa, Calif. for second place in the Aug. 18,
1963 200-mile when Gurney found himself faced with another challenge. This time it was Rodger Ward, Indi-
anapolis, Ind. (#1-Leader Card Spl.) who was after him. Gurney then spent the last 100 miles fending off Ward's
charges and managed to preserve his third place.

WHEN IRISH EYES ARE SMILING
COMELYS
When Irish eyes are smiling . . . sure and they'll belong to John Conely, Brighton, Mich. The 33 year old
veteran of 12 years in the racing wars stole the whole show here a year ago. He spun twice early in the 20-mile
added event and still came on to finish second. He then finished ninth in the 100-mile test, (spinning again on
the 93rd mile but managed to keep going) and the $1,000 prize money was the biggest single prize purse he'd
won in his racing career.

=== COLUMN 2 ===
It's a sad farewell we bid to Edward "Twenty
Grand" Steinbock, Chicago, who passed away Thurs-
day, April 23. Ed had been announcing races here
at state fair park since June, 1938. He was no new-
comer to racing. He drove a sprint car for a number
of years back in the 1920s on the tough northern
Illinois sprint car circuit. He earned the nickname
the same year "Twenty Grand" won the Kentucky
Derby. When he went through the fence in a race
and landed in a cornfield, somebody yelled, "Look
at old Twenty-Grand go for that corn."
"Twenty Grand" Steinbock was an announcer's
announcer. He kept meticulous records on all races
he covered. He knew racing from the ground up and
he could convey his knowledge. Auto racing will be
wanting because of his passing. He was a fine an-
nouncer, an excellent showman, and above all, a fine
gentleman.
Replacing "Twenty-Grand" is Myron Walden, a
staff announcer at WTMJ — The Milwaukee Journal.
Mike has been with the station since 1955. He's a
native of Springfield, Ill. and prior to coming here
was an announcer with the Illinois Sports Network
at Champaign.
Sports fans have heard Mike's broadcasts of
Green Bay Packer and University of Wisconsin foot-
5
ball; Milwaukee Braves baseball, and University of
Wisconsin basketball. While working for a small
station in Springfield, he handled a number of short
track broadcasting assignments. Mike's cheering sec-
tion is composed of wife, Nancy, and four youngsters
-Nanette, Greg, Julie, and David. The crew of
Wisconsin Auto Racing, Inc. welcomes you to state
fair park.
